title: Android LinearLayout: nested child baseline
purpose: Check that an Android XML LinearLayout can expose one nested child's text baseline so a neighboring item aligns with it.
changes: Added support for the Android baselineAlignedChildIndex attribute. A containing LinearLayout or RelativeLayout can use the chosen direct child's baseline. The example compares a nested layout with index 1 against one with no index.
steps: Turn on Show baseline alignment, then turn on Nested child baseline. Two rows with Caption, Nested and Peer should appear.
In the first row, the nested layout selects its second child (index 1). The words Nested and Peer should sit on the same imaginary baseline.
In the second row, no child index is set. Peer stays near the top of its row, noticeably higher than Nested.
Turn on Right-to-left layout. The order should reverse and the first row should still align Nested and Peer, while the second row remains unaligned.
Choose OK if the two rows behave as described. Otherwise choose Reject and explain what looks wrong, which row or direction is affected, and your device.
expected: With baselineAlignedChildIndex=1, the nested second child's baseline aligns with the neighboring Peer text. Without the index, the containing layout does not acquire that baseline. Right-to-left reverses order while preserving the relationship.
limits: This tests a nested vertical LinearLayout with two text children and a horizontal parent. XML handling and a RelativeLayout parent are also covered by automated tests. Android device font/pixel parity, nested weighted sizing, gravity and invalid-index exception parity remain open.

references.scope: Indexed child baseline propagation and vertical baseline offset behavior.

validation: All 155 Rust android_xml tests passed, including nested child baseline propagation into LinearLayout and RelativeLayout parents.
All 136 Android XML importer tests passed, including child index, unset value, invalid index syntax and unsupported tags.
Browser test-bhoo-linear-child-baseline.mjs passed rendered checks for the indexed and unindexed rows at 390px width, including RTL.
